title: Finite-Precision Certificates for Entropic Optimal-Transport Moment Criteria in Partial Identification
banked_reason: Exact rational minimum-cost flow already gives a stronger zero-width primal-dual certificate; the current assumptions provide no variable-dimension, parallel, or repeated-query regime proving a Sinkhorn-specific resource advantage.
gap_reasons: N-thin-survey — Tier=subfield below novelty_target=field: the survey omits exact rational min-cost-flow/transport certification (notably Orlin1993), so the stated certificate output has no demonstrated advantage over an established exact primal-dual route; a field claim needs a Sinkhorn-specific asymptotic, verification, or causal-decision advantage.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery attempted to turn the positive-temperature zero-set correction and certified Sinkhorn brackets into a field-tier computational certification result. The decisive comparison collapsed: exact rational min-cost flow already supplies a stronger zero-width primal-dual certificate in the stated fixed-dimensional regime. A viable follow-on would require a genuinely different regime with a proved Sinkhorn-specific asymptotic, parallel, amortized, or repeated-query advantage; that would be a new root claim rather than a revision.
tldr: The kernel asks whether an auditable finite-precision certificate for the original finite OT moment value can be constructed by composing directed rational enclosures for log-domain Sinkhorn and its generalized-KL dual with an accumulated-update budget, an explicit positivity floor, exact rational marginal repair, denominator and iteration bounds, and a polynomial total bit-work ledger. Boundary-valid minimax and entropy-selection identities show as supporting results that positive product-relative entropy collapses exact zero membership to the product coupling. Conditional on the certificate, global brackets combine with one finite multinomial event and polynomial separation to give simultaneous outer coverage and same-event Hausdorff control of the original sharp set.
gap: Regularized OT inference currently separates statistical validity, exact-real optimization complexity, and floating-point stability. None of the inspected results composes these layers into an outward certificate for the unregularized finite moment criterion.
fill: The project targets a seven-stage certificate joining directed elementary-function and generalized-KL dual enclosures, accumulated-update and positivity budgets, exact rational repair, denominator and iteration bounds, and a polynomial total bit-work ledger; the resulting bracket is then lifted across direction and parameter covers and propagated through a finite-sample outer-set theorem.
